messages:
Alex: Quick heads-up — our token-bucket enforcement blocked a 5% canary yesterday, ended up returning 503s. The canary traffic came in short spikes and drained the org bucket. Anyone seen similar?
Priya: Yup, saw alerts. We currently only have per-org + per-key buckets enforced at the gateway. Canaries are treated like normal traffic.
Tom: That's rough. Two quick options: ephemeral 'canary tokens' or switching the canary route to a leaky bucket for short windows. Both need strong telemetry.
Maya: Leaky bucket during rollout seems attractive — it smooths short bursts instead of letting a bucket exhaust immediately. Could be config-driven: route-level burst window + temporary refill multiplier.
Alex: Prototype config sketch I wrote locally: 
```
route:
  id: payment-create
  burst_window: 30s
  burst_capacity: 1000
  enforcement: per-org
  canary_override:
    enabled: true
    mode: leaky
    extra_tokens: 200
    ttl: 60s
```
Priya: A couple of concerns: 1) abuse — what prevents a customer from pretending to be a canary to get higher bursts? 2) accounting — if we hand out extra tokens, how do we reconcile billing and quota dashboards?
Elena: For telemetry we should emit: burst_override_applied, tokens_granted_by_override, rollout_id tag on traces, and X-RateLimit-Mode header so logs can filter canary flows.
Sam: Operational constraint: we must guard overrides with pool_utilization checks. If GPU pools are >70% utilized, overrides should be denied automatically. Can't raise burst capacity when infra is saturated.
Tom: Also think about a short optimistic replenishment: allow a small 'prefetch' credit that is reclaimed if not used within N seconds. That helps clients that prefetch embeddings. Add a reclamation metric.
Maya: Edge case: fallback paths. If canary hits capacity and falls back to a smaller model, ensure we don't double-charge tokens — update accounting so fallback consumes from the same logical request token envelope.
Priya: Security: require rollout_flag signed by platform (not client) and record rollout_id in audit log. Also require that canary_override only applies to routes with explicit rollout metadata.
Alex: OK. Summary action items: 1) I'll open a tiny gateway PR implementing canary_override + leaky-mode switch, with the config above. 2) Elena to add the telemetry counters and trace tags. 3) Sam to add the util < 70% precondition and an emergency kill switch. 4) Priya to write the safety doc covering abuse/billing.
Elena: I'll also add a small sampling to capture token usage before/after override so we can validate the model change doesn't hide real usage.
Sam: For rollout gating, suggest bot-enforced policy: infra-bot denies enabling override unless 'pool_utilization:<70' check passes.
infra-bot: deploy-checklist: new config fields detected (canary_override, burst_window). Ensure gateway feature flag added and migrations tested.
Alex: I'll target a PR today and ping this thread. If implemented, this should reduce canary-induced 503s while preserving safety. :thumbsup:
Priya: Thanks — let's keep the change small and observable. If we see regressions revert fast.
__note: No title field per agents.md. Thread messages are a single continuous string with senders prefixed.
